explanation: Its pyramid has four stairways. Near the March and September equinoxes, the afternoon sun casts a shadow like a serpent's body down the northern steps.

claims.text: Chichén Itzá was not built by the Aztecs, the Zapotecs or the Olmecs.
El Castillo at Chichén Itzá has four stairways.
Near the March and September equinoxes, afternoon sunlight casts a serpent-like shadow down El Castillo's northern stairway.

evidence.restatement: Chichén Itzá is a Maya city in the north of the Yucatán peninsula.
The Aztecs and Zapotecs lived in central and southern Mexico and the Olmecs flourished far earlier on the Gulf Coast; none of them built Chichén Itzá.
El Castillo, the Temple of Kukulcan, has a stairway up each of its four sides.

evidence.restatement: Around the spring and autumn equinoxes the late-afternoon sun throws a zigzag of light and shade down the balustrade of the northern stairway, read as a descending serpent.
Chichén Itzá, in Yucatán, was a Maya city.
The Aztecs ruled from central Mexico, the Zapotecs lived in Oaxaca and the Olmecs on the Gulf Coast, and none built Chichén Itzá.
El Castillo has a stairway on each of its four faces.
